To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel joint embedding framework for multi-cue zero-shot learning; (2) we demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the art by a large margin on the challenging CUB-200-2011 dataset; and (3) we show that our framework is also able to improve the performance on a challenging zero-shot retrieval task.

(1) we can learn to transfer knowledge from a large number of source classes with a limited number of training examples by leveraging a variety of auxiliary information from the web, and (2) we can achieve state-of-the-art results on zero-shot recognition and retrieval by incorporating stronger supervision in the transfer learning framework.

(i) multi-cue zero-shot learning with weak supervision is a promising approach to scale up visual category recognition and (ii) the combination of multiple text sources with stronger supervision in the visual space is a promising approach towards this goal.

two main aspects: 1) How can we use the large amounts of unstructured text on the web to obtain a richer description of visual classes, which can be used for zero-shot learning?
